To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the content-addressable memory can be realized by a physical system with emergent collective properties of use to biological organisms or to computers, and that the physical meaning of content-addressable memory is described in terms of an appropriate phase-space flow.

(1) The content addressable memory (CAM) of the brain can be described in terms of a phase space flow, (2) the phase space flow can be modeled as an asynchronous parallel processor, (3) the model is based on the properties of neurons, (4) the model can be implemented in integrated circuits.
A) A content addressable memory can be constructed using a large number of identical components, each of which is simple enough that it can be built using integrated circuit techniques.

the development of a theory of computation in physical systems, and in particular with the study of the collective computational properties of systems having many simple equivalent elements.

a large number of neurons can collectively perform a task that a few neurons cannot do individually, and that the emergent properties of the collective are robust to the failure of individual neurons.
